---

## Story Goal

Ship a self-serve Knowledge Base that lets agents author help content and customers search it. Deliverables:

1. Agents (staff) can create, edit, publish, unpublish and delete **articles** organised into **categories** with a `kind` distinguishing **FAQ**, **help article**, and **solution/guide**.
2. Public/portal users can list published articles by category, open an article by slug, and run **keyword search** across title, summary and body.
3. Agent-side search endpoint returns drafts + published; portal search returns only published articles.
4. Agent-side UI (React) with a Knowledge Base list page, article editor, and category management. Portal-side UI adds a browse + search page and a read view.

**Out of scope:** article versioning/revision history, per-article ACL beyond published/unpublished, rich HTML sanitisation beyond storing markdown, translations, article feedback/ratings (may be added later), analytics beyond a simple `view_count`.

### 1 — Data model

Create file: `backend/app/models/knowledge_base.py`

Declare two SQLAlchemy models using the existing `Base` from `app.db.base`. **Every table in this codebase keys on `uuid.UUID` via the shared `_pk()` helper** (`backend/app/models/customer.py:44-45`, `mapped_column(Uuid, primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)`) — there is no integer-PK table anywhere to mirror instead. Import `_pk` from `app.models.customer` the same way `backend/app/models/agent.py:43` does.

- **`ArticleCategory`** — table `kb_article_categories`

  - `slug: Mapped[str]` unique, indexed, max 128

  - `id: Mapped[uuid.UUID]` = `_pk()`

  - `body: Mapped[str]` (text; markdown source)

  - `status: Mapped[str]` values `"draft" | "published"` default `"draft"`, indexed

  - `published_at: Mapped[datetime | None]`
  - `created_at`, `updated_at: Mapped[datetime]`

### 3 — Pydantic schemas

Create file: `backend/app/schemas/knowledge_base.py`

Define with Pydantic v2 (`ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)`):

Ids are `uuid.UUID` throughout, matching every other schema module (`backend/app/schemas/agent.py:3-4`: "Ids are `uuid.UUID` throughout, matching every other table in this codebase").

```python
class ArticleCategoryBase(BaseModel):
    slug: str
    name: str
    description: str | None = None
    sort_order: int = 0

class ArticleCategoryCreate(ArticleCategoryBase): ...
class ArticleCategoryUpdate(BaseModel):
    slug: str | None = None
    name: str | None = None
    description: str | None = None
    sort_order: int | None = None

class ArticleCategoryRead(ArticleCategoryBase):
    id: uuid.UUID
    created_at: datetime
    updated_at: datetime
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

class ArticleBase(BaseModel):
    slug: str
    title: str
    summary: str | None = None
    body: str
    kind: Literal["faq", "help", "guide"]
    status: Literal["draft", "published"] = "draft"
    category_id: uuid.UUID | None = None

class ArticleCreate(ArticleBase): ...
class ArticleUpdate(BaseModel):
    slug: str | None = None
    title: str | None = None
    summary: str | None = None
    body: str | None = None
    kind: Literal["faq", "help", "guide"] | None = None
    status: Literal["draft", "published"] | None = None
    category_id: uuid.UUID | None = None

class ArticleRead(ArticleBase):
    id: uuid.UUID
    view_count: int
    published_at: datetime | None
    created_at: datetime
    updated_at: datetime
    category: ArticleCategoryRead | None = None
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

class ArticleSummary(BaseModel):
    id: uuid.UUID
    slug: str
    title: str
    summary: str | None
    kind: Literal["faq", "help", "guide"]
    category_id: uuid.UUID | None
    updated_at: datetime
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
```

### 4 — Service layer

Create file: `backend/app/services/knowledge_base.py`

Functions (all take `session: Session` first):

- **Categories:** `list_categories`, `get_category(id_or_slug)`, `create_category`, `update_category`, `delete_category` (SET NULL cascades from DB; forbid delete if articles remain unless `force=True`; default: reject with `Conflict` if present — see `errors.py`).
- **Articles (staff):** `list_articles(*, kind=None, status=None, category_id=None, q=None, limit, offset)`, `get_article(id_or_slug)`, `create_article`, `update_article`, `publish_article`, `unpublish_article`, `delete_article`.
- **Articles (public):** `list_public_articles(*, kind=None, category_slug=None, q=None, limit, offset)`, `get_public_article_by_slug(slug)` — filter `status == "published"`, auto-increment `view_count` inside `get_public_article_by_slug` and return the refreshed record.
- **Search:** implement `q` as case-insensitive `ILIKE` (Postgres) fall-back to `LIKE` for SQLite tests, covering `title`, `summary`, `body`. Order by `updated_at DESC` when no query, else by an ILIKE-in-title-first heuristic (title match first, then summary, then body).

Publishing must set `published_at = datetime.utcnow()` the first time an article moves from `draft` → `published` (idempotent — do not overwrite if already published). Unpublishing does **not** clear `published_at`.

Use `errors.NotFound` and `errors.Conflict` from `backend/app/services/errors.py` (`backend/app/services/errors.py:10-15` — the classes are named `NotFound`/`Conflict`, **not** `NotFoundError`/`ConflictError`) for missing rows and duplicate slugs.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Duplicate slug on create/update** — service raises `Conflict`; API returns HTTP 409 (mapped centrally in `backend/app/main.py` alongside `NotFound`/`Forbidden`/`PayloadTooLarge`). Enforced in the unique index on `kb_articles.slug` / `kb_article_categories.slug` and in `create_article` / `update_article` in `backend/app/services/knowledge_base.py`.
- **Delete category that still has articles** — service raises `Conflict` unless `?force=true`; force sets `category_id = NULL` on children via ON DELETE SET NULL.
- **Publish an article with empty body** — reject in service with HTTP 422 (`body` required non-empty on transition to `published`).
- **Portal request for a draft article by slug** — return HTTP 404 from `get_public_article_by_slug` (do not leak existence of drafts).
- **Search with empty `q`** — treat as no filter (do not apply an `ILIKE %%`).
- **Unicode / accented terms in `q`** — rely on `ILIKE` (Postgres) for case-insensitive matching; document that diacritics are not stripped.
- **Concurrent `view_count` increment** — use `UPDATE ... SET view_count = view_count + 1` (SQL-level increment) rather than read-modify-write to avoid lost updates.
- **Migration on a half-applied DB** — `downgrade()` must drop `kb_articles` before `kb_article_categories` (FK order).
- **Frontend: markdown renderer not installed** — render as `<pre>` and log a TODO; do not attempt raw HTML injection.
- **Navigation regression** — updating `App.tsx` / `PortalApp.tsx` must not break existing routes; run `frontend/src/__tests__/navigation.test.tsx` after changes.

## Migration / Rollback

- Migration file `0006_knowledge_base.py`, with `revision = '0006'` and `down_revision = '0005'` (bare numbers, matching every prior migration's revision-id style).
- Apply with `alembic upgrade head` from `backend/`.
- Rollback with `alembic downgrade -1` — will drop both tables. Verify order (`kb_articles` before `kb_article_categories`).
- **Half-applied state:** if the migration fails midway (e.g. articles created but categories not), Alembic runs each migration in a transaction on Postgres; SQLite falls back to non-transactional. For SQLite dev DBs, drop the DB file and re-run `alembic upgrade head`.
- No data backfill required (new tables are empty).

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `cd backend && uv run alembic upgrade head` — migration applies cleanly.
2. **Backend tests:** `cd backend && uv run pytest -q` — all existing tests still pass, new KB tests pass.
3. **Backend serves:** `cd backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload` — hit `GET /api/kb/articles` (with agent auth) and `GET /api/portal/kb/articles` (no auth) and inspect JSON.
4. **Frontend runs:** `cd frontend && npm run dev` — open `/kb` (agent) and `/portal/kb` (portal); create an article, publish it, verify it appears in portal search.
5. **Frontend tests:** `cd frontend && npm test` — new and existing suites green.
6. **Regression:** run `pytest -q` and `npm test`; open the dashboard and portal pages to confirm no navigation breakage.
